MEASURED the 041122 page spill, and it is not a paragraph property. Rendered-row heights vs declared trHeight on table 17 (24 rows, sum 16649tw=832pt): row1 23.2/23.15 ok, row2 93.1/84.1 (+9), rows3-15 ok, row16-18 ok, row19 37.6/29.15 (+8.5), row20 61.7/41 (+20.7), row21-22 ok, row23 340.4/231.5 (+109) -> spills to our p9, row24 41.6/41.35 ok. The growing rows grow by WHOLE LINES, not by w:before or w:line: row23 has 20 source lines and renders 26, each 'before' is 0-4pt and line is exact 240tw=12pt, exactly the source's 12pt pitch. Cause is a WRAP: the reference renderer has no Effra, substitutes Noto Sans, and 'Verification' at 10pt measures 61.24pt against Effra's 52.40pt (+16.9%), while the cell leaves only 2.5pt of slack (source line ends x=568.8, cell edge 571.9 = 0.5%). Every full-width source line therefore wraps its tail. Ruled out: w:before/w:after (sum 24pt, not 109), w:line exact (12pt = source pitch), cantSplit (present but only moves an already-taller row), the pieces index and the sizePt bug (both fixed, re-verified: row1's six heading lines carry 9452/4255/4705/3830/107/2079 and render at declared height). Also measured: our p7 blank page is NOT table 17 - it is page 6's page furniture (blue heading bar + footer rule + page number at y=-7.5) whose anchor paragraphs were pushed off page 6. No engine change yet this attempt.

Carry-over premise DISPROVED by measurement, not a code change. (1) The source's own pitch in the verification cell of 041122 p7 is exactly 12.00 pt: PyMuPDF baselines 579.61,591.61,603.61,615.61 -> deltas 12.00,12.00,12.00, and the 240 tw w:line we already write IS that pitch. The row's 4630 tw is not '20 lines x 11.6': it is 16 lines at 240 tw + 5 paragraph gaps (w:before sums 562 tw) = 4642 tw written against 4630 declared, i.e. 0.6 pt, exact. Changing the cell box to 231.5/20=11.575 pt would make every line 0.425 pt too tight and the block 6.4 pt short. (2) The rendered overflow is NOT the line box: each of the 16 source lines is re-wrapped into 2 by the reader, so r23 renders 26 lines x 12 pt = 312 pt against 231.5 declared (+80.5). (3) The cause is the face: the PDF names Effra, the reader substitutes NotoSans-Regular, and that string is 10.5 pct wider (source line 'above is true...' 526.5 pt; ours needs ~582 in a 531.8 tw cell with 3.9 pt of slack). RULED OUT this run: w:noWrap on the cell (added to tcPr of the 20-line row, re-rendered: identical 12 pages, identical wraps - LibreOffice ignores it for line breaking); cell pitch (measured exact); trHeight/hRule (atLeast, and content = 4642 vs 4630). The remaining lever is face fidelity (embed the PDF subset, or condense), which is a multi-run change and not a one-line pitch edit.

The page's own advance widths are now carried in a face the reader has. DocxWriter writes a run in Arial (which LibreOffice supplies as Liberation Sans, metric-identical) with w:w set to the scale that reproduces the width the page drew, whenever the PDF's face is not one the reader is guaranteed to have. Measured on 041122: 12 -> 11 pages; source page 6's folio stays on page 6 (it was at y=-7.5 on a sheet of its own), source page 7's table now fits at 795.2 pt against the page's own 800.4 (it was splitting across two sheets). The twin Account_Opening_Form_Fillable_filled is 11 pages by the same structure. Ruled out by measurement this run: the carry-over's pitch premise (source baselines are 12.00 pt exactly, the 240 tw w:line is right, the 4630 tw row is 16 lines + 562 tw of gaps), an embedded font part (LibreOffice ignores it: 12 pages, NotoSans, identical geometry), w:fitText (ignored), and w:noWrap (ignored for line breaking). Guard: the mechanism is a no-op for any face in the allowlist (Arial/Helvetica/Liberation/DejaVu/Noto/Times/Courier/Calibri/Cambria/Georgia/Verdana/Tahoma/Symbol/Webdings), with PDF subset tags stripped, so the 211-document synthetic corpus - all DejaVu - cannot be touched by construction. NOT YET DONE: gate.py --budget 250 over the whole corpus, so this is not a committed ratchet yet; and the last spurious page on 041122 is the page-7 folio, which the model emits as a TABLE CELL (TableText paragraph), not a flow line - the folio rule added this run only reaches flow lines.

A page's folio is not a row of the table the page's rules bound. On 041122 page 7 the ruled pass hands the folio '7' back as the table's LAST row (the row between the content rule at y=800.4 and the page's foot frame; its only text is the sheet number). Written as a row it is charged its whole band (827 tw, 41.4 pt) on a page whose content already ends at 800.4 of 842, so the renderer breaks the sheet and the folio costs a page of its own. DocxWriter.table() now detects a trailing row that is only a folio with its baseline in the page's bottom band (>0.88 page height) and emits it as an anchored line at its own x/y (the treatment the flow folio rule already gives), with the table ending at the row edge the page's content ends on. 041122: 11 pages -> 10, source 9. Proof of no regression: all 213 documents re-converted with the patched engine and compared entry-by-entry inside the .docx - 212 of 213 are byte-identical in every zip entry, so their renders and scores are unchanged; only 041122 differs. Doc share5 97.62 -> 86.25 (worst page 7 -> 9), text_recall unchanged. Remaining extra page is the instruction page's 17-line spill (our p9), untouched by this patch.
